source.title: Governance Standard for Islamic Financial Institutions No. 8 - Central Shari'ah Board

display_card: GS 8: Central Shari'ah Board (CSB) - appointment, composition, functions, independence of jurisdiction-level Shari'ah boards
applicability: Applies to governance for CSBs or similar bodies that oversee and advise on Shari'ah matters to regulators and government authorities (para 3).
Does NOT apply to Shari'ah supervisory boards (SSBs) or other institution-level boards/committees; those are covered by separate standards (para 4, referencing GSIFI 1 and 4).
Two CSB types recognized: national Shari'ah board and regulatory Shari'ah board (para 5b, footnotes 2-3).
Standard encourages but does not mandate creation of CSBs (PR7); does not prefer centralized over non-centralized model (PR5).
core_machinery: Appointment: first appointment, subsequent appointments, nomination committee, remuneration, terms of reference (paras 6-13).
Tenure and re-appointments: recommended 3-5 year term, rotation policy (paras 14-15).
Composition and selection: scholar vs expert members, minimum member counts, chairman/vice-chairman election, quorum rules, diversity (paras 16-24).
Removal and termination: grounds and due process (para 25).
Functions: Fatwas, advisory, regulations, oversight/limited supervision (paras 26-33).
Other functional provisions: decisions, secretariat, self-evaluation and reporting, confidentiality (paras 34-44).
Fit and proper criteria for Shari'ah scholar members and expert members (paras 46-50).
Independence: considerations for selection/appointment and for functioning (paras 51-54).
implications: Aims to reduce conflicting Fatwas/rulings across IFIs in a jurisdiction, increasing industry credibility and client/investor confidence (PR3, IN3).
CSBs expected to adopt AAOIFI Shari'ah Standards and follow Shari'ah Standard No. 29 on Fatwa ethics (PR6).
CSB functions are primarily advisory/reactive; proactive action only when specific conditions in para 31(a-c) are all met.
Decisions relating to advisory/Fatwa functions, with basis of conclusion, are to be compiled and published regularly subject to legal/regulatory constraints (para 37).
Annual self-evaluation and performance reporting to appointing authority required (paras 41-42); public disclosure to be mutually agreed (para 43).
limitations: Standard encourages but does not mandate formation of CSBs (PR7).
Does not apply to SSBs or institution-level boards (para 4).
Does not favor centralized vs non-centralized model (PR5).
Cooling-off period for re-appointment left to appointing authority's discretion (para 15, confirmed BC7).
"Professional misconduct" (ground for removal) intentionally left undefined (para 25a, BC13).
disputes: BC1: rationale for need of a CSB.
BC2: need for individual SSBs alongside CSB.
BC3: nomination committee formation as good governance practice.
BC4: cooling-off period for re-appointments left to appointing authority.
BC5: engagement of experts and voting rights split (Shari'ah rulings reserved to scholar members; other matters equal voting).
BC6: functions of the CSB - advisory/Fatwa vs full supervisory role rejected.
BC8: number of CSB meetings left to each CSB's discretion.
BC9: removal/termination - "professional misconduct" left undefined deliberately.
BC10: reporting and disclosure - report to appointing authority mandatory.
BC11: making the report public and disclosing remuneration decided to be mandatory.
BC12-BC16 (as numbered in Appendix B, e.g. independence exemptions per para 51(c)-(d)).

timeline_bridge.transitional_provision: Applies to terms of reference, appointment, constitution/reconstitution events occurring on or after effective date (para 56)
timeline_bridge.adoption: Approved in AAOIFI Governance and Ethics Board meeting No. 5, 22-23 Dhul-Qa'dah 1438H / 15-16 August 2017 (Appendix A)
